ideas.title: Compile shopping requests into verified hard constraints
ideas.buyer: Camera-accessory, computer-peripheral and specialist equipment retailers with frequent compatibility questions.
ideas.problem: Semantic retrieval can return plausible items that violate one decisive requirement, while ordinary filters miss requirements expressed in a sentence.
ideas.mechanism: Selection stage: translate an explicit request into testable requirements, eliminate verified mismatches and expose unresolved facts. More shoppers can reach a defensible suitable choice and complete a retained purchase. External discovery improves only if an approved channel actually uses the resulting data or tool.
ideas.intervention: Build a constraint compiler with typed units, model/version relations and three states per predicate: supported, contradicted or unknown. Return an evidence-backed candidate set, its smallest conflicting constraint set when empty, and explicit alternatives the shopper can approve. Start with one category and a merchant-controlled AI landing page or retrieval endpoint.
ideas.competitorOverlap: Constructor ASA already handles natural-language filtering and refinement; constraint-based knowledge-graph recommenders exist. Constructor also advertises Answer Engine Assistants beta. A natural-language filter or generic compatibility badge is not the edge.
ideas.edgeHypothesis: For requests with several hard requirements, verified relational constraints and an explicit unknown state outperform a well-configured incumbent semantic search plus facets on retained purchases without excessive false exclusions.
dataNeeded: Consented shopper request or explicit handoff context
SKU and variant identities, canonical units and manufacturer compatibility relations
Source provenance and recency for each decisive predicate
Assigned-user orders, cancellations and returns
ideas.experiment: Persistently randomize eligible shoppers before results between the compiler and the merchant's strongest configured search/facet experience. Enroll all requests identified as constraint-bearing before assignment. Primary endpoint is a paid purchase within 14 days retained through day 45; use 6-8 weeks of enrollment plus maturation, with sample size set from the merchant baseline and minimum worthwhile effect. Guardrails: incompatible recommendations, false exclusions, latency and contribution per shopper.
ideas.metric: ITT difference in retained-purchaser probability: unique assigned shoppers with at least one retained order divided by every eligible assigned shopper. Count all merchant purchases in the category, not just purchases of the promoted candidate. Report AI-referral and merchant-assistant cohorts separately.
ideas.impactEvidence: Hypothesized purchase effect. constraint-paper supports technical feasibility; ecom-bench supports a requirement-level offline test design only; constructor-asa and constructor-home establish overlap. No direct conversion percentage is supported.

impactScenario.baseline: No observed traffic or conversion baseline. Chosen sensitivity: GBP40 contribution per additional retained purchaser; GBP600 recurring monthly fee plus operation cost.
impactScenario.calculation: Break-even requires 600/40 = 15 additional retained purchasers monthly, or an absolute rate change of 15/N for N eligible monthly shoppers. Add amortized integration costs to the numerator. Zero lift loses GBP600; false exclusions can make the purchase effect negative.

ideas.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated value-based test price: GBP500/month plus separately quoted integration. Require a paid pilot; no published demand estimate is asserted.
ideas.costControl: Use deterministic predicates after one parse, cache stable compatibility edges and reserve model calls for unresolved language. Never reuse cached stock or price without a valid freshness policy.
dependencies: Accurate category ontology and variant-level source evidence
Merchant-controlled retrieval or landing experience
Enough eligible purchase volume to compare against incumbent search
ideas.failureMode: Bad mappings reject good products, missing specifications create empty results, or an extra verification step adds more friction than it removes.
ideas.falsifier: Reject the claim if a powered test rules out the minimum worthwhile retained-purchase increase, or verified incompatibility/false-exclusion guardrails worsen. Better simulated constraint satisfaction alone does not rescue it.

ideas.title: Ask only the question that can change the purchase decision
ideas.buyer: Retailers of considered purchases whose AI shoppers frequently arrive with incomplete requirements.
ideas.problem: A chatbot can ask many reasonable questions that do not change the candidate set, while failing to ask the one question that prevents a wrong or abandoned purchase.
ideas.mechanism: Selection stage: estimate whether one answer would change the suitable shortlist enough to justify the shopper's effort. A useful clarification should reduce a material mismatch or comparison burden before the shopper leaves.
ideas.intervention: Build a question-selection policy that compares expected decision regret with the predicted cost of an extra turn. Candidate actions include asking one bounded question, showing a small provisional shortlist, or proceeding. Ask only for task-relevant preferences, offer 'not sure', and expose why the answer matters.
ideas.competitorOverlap: Constructor ASA already supports conversational refinement. Research already studies appropriate question selection. This proposal is a narrow policy within those experiences, not a new chatbot category.
ideas.edgeHypothesis: A policy trained on randomized real-user responses and retained purchases asks fewer irrelevant questions and produces more retained purchasers than either a fixed questionnaire or unrestricted LLM conversation.
dataNeeded: Pre-question request and current feasible candidate set
Candidate question, answerability and response-time estimates
Logged action probabilities from consented live exploration
Shopper answers, abandonment, paid orders and returns
ideas.experiment: Randomize eligible shoppers at their first ambiguous request to decision-value questioning, the existing assistant, or a brief fixed questionnaire. Keep product coverage and incentives equal. Use 6-8 weeks of enrollment plus a 45-day return window; power the main comparison for retained purchasers, not response rate. Cap questions and monitor latency, abandonment and unsuitable orders.
ideas.metric: Retained purchasers within the prespecified 14-day purchase window divided by all assigned ambiguous-intent shoppers, including those who never answer. Report question-answer rate as a diagnostic only. Category-wide purchase measurement catches simple switching between suggested SKUs.
ideas.impactEvidence: Hypothesized. question-paper and ecom-bench provide adjacent question-selection and scripted-intent evaluation precedents. Neither measures this policy's incremental human purchases.

impactScenario.baseline: No measured baseline. Assume solely for break-even GBP40 contribution per extra retained purchaser and GBP500/month total recurring cost.
impactScenario.calculation: 500/40 = 12.5, so at least 13 additional retained purchasers per month are needed before setup costs. Required absolute rate gain is 12.5/N. Unhelpful questions can reduce purchases; zero gain leaves the full cost uncovered.

ideas.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated value-based test price: GBP400/month for a category pilot, with integration priced separately.
ideas.costControl: Precompute answerable questions and shortlist partitions; stop after one useful question unless the shopper requests more help.
dependencies: An assistant or landing experience the merchant can change
Observable candidate-set differences between possible answers
Sufficient real purchase labels and randomized action logs
ideas.failureMode: The value model confuses engagement with buying intent, asks an intrusive question, or expects shoppers to know technical details they cannot answer.
ideas.falsifier: Drop the approach if it cannot outperform a one-question heuristic on retained purchases at acceptable abandonment, or if any measured benefit disappears when question count and latency are matched.

ideas.title: Solve the complete purchase mission before recommending a basket
ideas.buyer: DIY, hobby, office-setup and consumer-electronics retailers selling complementary components.
ideas.problem: Individually attractive recommendations can form an unusable or over-budget basket: a missing adapter, duplicate component, incompatible connector or invalid discount prevents completion.
ideas.mechanism: Selection and cart stages: satisfy a whole task with the minimum complete set of compatible items and a checked total. Removing missing-component and budget uncertainty can convert shoppers who would otherwise abandon a project purchase.
ideas.intervention: Build a graph and constraint solver over component roles, pairwise compatibility, ownership supplied by the shopper, available variants, taxes/fees and valid promotions. Return a complete minimum-cost feasible basket plus optional upgrades separately. Revalidate against authoritative cart totals before checkout.
ideas.competitorOverlap: Constructor already supports goal-based multi-item recommendations, and Algolia has strict co-purchase bundles. Native cart tools already exist. The proposed difference is deterministic mission completion and budget feasibility, not displaying several products or creating a cart.
ideas.edgeHypothesis: For multi-item missions, a verified complete basket yields more retained purchasing shoppers than the incumbent agent or co-purchase recommender while reducing missing-component support and returns.
dataNeeded: Task templates and necessary component roles
Compatibility and exclusion edges with provenance
Shopper-declared already-owned components
Live stock, authoritative cart quotes, discount rules and order/refund data
ideas.experiment: Randomize mission-bearing shoppers before recommendations between solver-generated baskets and the merchant's current goal-based assistant. Keep promotional eligibility equal. Run 8 weeks or the powered sample target, then follow orders through the category's return window. Primary endpoint is a retained purchaser within 14 days; guardrails include incompatible basket rate, over-budget quotes, refunds and margin.
ideas.metric: All assigned mission shoppers form the denominator. Compare retained-purchaser probability and separately the proportion with a complete verified mission basket. Do not present increased items per order or AOV as increased purchase conversion.
ideas.impactEvidence: Hypothesized. combo-bench offers a simulated evaluation structure; constructor-asa and algolia-fbt show strong direct overlap. No cited source demonstrates our incremental purchase rate.

impactScenario.baseline: No measured traffic/conversion. Chosen values: GBP60 incremental contribution per retained purchasing shopper and GBP1,500/month total recurring cost.
impactScenario.calculation: 1,500/60 = 25 extra retained purchasing shoppers per month before setup. Absolute break-even rate gain is 25/N. Existing buyers adding components are secondary value, not counted as newly converted purchasers. Zero or negative purchaser effects remain possible.

ideas.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated value-based test price: GBP1,000/month plus category modelling and cart integration.
ideas.costControl: Restrict the first release to a few repeatable missions; use integer/constraint solving and cached compatibility rather than repeated open-ended model reasoning.
dependencies: Category expert to validate mission templates
Reliable compatibility data
Live cart quote and inventory integration
Enough multi-item mission traffic
ideas.failureMode: The system invents a necessary component, omits an adapter, over-constrains the basket or pressures shoppers into buying extras they already own.
ideas.falsifier: Kill the conversion claim if the solver improves basket validity but yields no worthwhile retained-purchaser gain, or the incumbent assistant reaches equivalent results at materially lower cost.

ideas.title: Recover stockouts with an explicit substitute-versus-wait policy
ideas.buyer: Merchants with high variant turnover and AI referrals to products that become unavailable.
ideas.problem: A generic similar-products carousel may miss the requirement that made a shopper choose an unavailable item, or divert a shopper who would have bought the original after a short wait.
ideas.mechanism: Landing and selection stages: identify which properties are essential, then choose between a verified substitute, a genuinely available alternate variant, or a truthful wait option. The policy seeks additional retained shoppers after a stockout while accounting for purchases merely moved forward in time.
ideas.intervention: Build a conditional substitution graph with shopper-visible differences and protected requirements. Use restock uncertainty, explicit deadline, delivered cost and historic accepted substitutions to choose a small recovery set. Preserve the original item and let the shopper explicitly approve any relaxed preference.
ideas.competitorOverlap: Algolia already recommends alternatives to out-of-stock items and supports stock filters. This is a decision policy over substitute, variant and wait options, with longer-horizon cannibalization measurement, not an out-of-stock carousel invention.
ideas.edgeHypothesis: On failed AI arrivals, requirement-preserving recovery produces more retained purchasers over 60 days than strong related-product recommendations, rather than merely shifting orders away from the original SKU or a later visit.
dataNeeded: Unavailable exact variant and timestamp
Explicit shopper requirements and deadline where supplied
Live substitute inventory and credible restock estimates
Accepted/rejected substitutions and 60-day customer-level purchase histories
ideas.experiment: Persistently randomize shoppers at the first verified stockout between policy recovery and the existing related-products/waitlist experience. Run 6-8 weeks plus 60-day follow-up; size from stockout-cohort volume. Primary endpoint is a retained purchasing shopper over the whole 60-day horizon. Guardrails: unsuitable replacements, higher returns, misleading restock promises and lost margin.
ideas.metric: Unique retained purchasers across all merchant SKUs divided by every assigned stockout shopper. Report near-term rescue orders separately from 60-day incrementality. An order for the substitute alone does not prove a saved sale.
ideas.impactEvidence: Hypothesized policy effect; algolia-stockout and algolia-rules establish direct competition. assortment-paper supports modelling substitution but supplies no live AI-origin conversion estimate.

impactScenario.baseline: No observed fault prevalence or baseline. Chosen sensitivity: GBP35 contribution per truly additional retained shopper and GBP700/month total recurring cost.
impactScenario.calculation: 700/35 = 20 additional retained shoppers in the stockout cohort each month before integration cost. Rate threshold is 20/N_stockout. If substitution only cannibalizes later purchases, incremental value is zero before cost; poor substitutions can make it negative.

ideas.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated value-based test price: GBP500/month; qualify merchants on actual stockout traffic before selling.
ideas.costControl: Precompute proven substitute edges and evaluate only currently available options. Do not spend inference on stockouts with no useful recovery action.
dependencies: Reliable variant-level inventory and restock information
Customer assignment durable enough for long-horizon measurement
Merchant control of the stockout landing experience
ideas.failureMode: The substitute violates an unstated hard requirement, inaccurate restock estimates distort the choice, or the system takes credit for a purchase that would have happened later.
ideas.falsifier: Reject if the 60-day all-SKU retained-purchaser effect fails the minimum worthwhile threshold despite a higher immediate substitute-order rate.

ideas.title: Turn room images into a conservative physical-fit decision
ideas.buyer: Furniture and storage merchants receiving AI-origin shoppers with a specific space constraint.
ideas.problem: Visual similarity and attractive room renders do not resolve whether a real item fits through an opening, leaves requested clearance or fits inside a recess.
ideas.mechanism: Selection stage: combine explicitly supplied measurements or a consented scan with product geometry and uncertainty bounds. A verifiable fit decision can resolve hesitation and prevent unsuitable orders, producing more retained purchases.
ideas.intervention: Create a bounded geometry checker for a narrow use case such as shelving inside an alcove. Accept manual dimensions or supported room scans, carry measurement uncertainty, test product/packaging dimensions and requested clearance, and abstain when margin is insufficient. Render the checked measurements beside the product; ask the shopper to confirm critical dimensions.
ideas.competitorOverlap: IKEA Kreativ already scans or builds rooms and places products at scale. Apple RoomPlan already supplies parametric geometry. The edge must be better decision accuracy and checkout outcomes for a specific fit task across a merchant's assortment, not another room visualization.
ideas.edgeHypothesis: For shoppers with a narrow spatial requirement, uncertainty-aware fit checking beats an incumbent scaled visualization plus dimension table on retained-purchaser rate and fit-related refunds.
dataNeeded: Consented scan or manually entered dimensions
Product and packaging dimensions with measurement tolerances
Explicit clearance requirement and candidate placement
Verified fit outcomes, retained orders and fit-related return reasons
ideas.experiment: Randomize eligible AI-origin landing visitors before the fit-tool invitation to checker versus current visualizer/dimension table. Count non-users of the offered tool in treatment. Use 8-12 weeks and a 60-day post-order return window; high-value low-frequency categories may require multiple merchants. Primary endpoint is a retained purchase; guardrails include false-fit decisions, scan burden, abandonment and privacy complaints.
ideas.metric: Retained purchasers within 30 days divided by all assigned eligible shoppers, with the category's return window matured. Secondary fit-error rate uses independently checked measurements; do not substitute render engagement for purchases.
ideas.impactEvidence: Hypothesized. apple-roomplan establishes building blocks and ikea-kreativ direct competition. Neither supports our conversion estimate or a universal accuracy guarantee.

impactScenario.baseline: No observed traffic/conversion. Chosen sensitivity: GBP150 contribution per extra retained purchaser and GBP2,000/month total recurring cost.
impactScenario.calculation: 2,000/150 = 13.34, so at least 14 additional retained purchasers monthly before integration and measurement costs. Absolute rate threshold is 13.34/N. Reduced unsuitable orders may lower gross orders while improving retained orders; scan friction can make both negative.

ideas.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated value-based test price: GBP1,500/month plus scan/geometry integration, appropriate only for merchants with enough relevant demand.
ideas.costControl: Start with manual dimensions and simple bounding geometry; invoke scanning or richer geometry only when it can change a purchase decision. Never present photorealistic rendering as measurement evidence.
dependencies: Trustworthy product and package measurements
Browser measurement flow or optional supported mobile scan
Merchant agreement on tolerances and an explicit abstention policy
ideas.failureMode: Photos lack scale, scans miss obstacles, product dimensions exclude protrusions, or the visual confidence of the interface exceeds the evidence.
ideas.falsifier: Stop if independent checks find unacceptable false-fit rates, or a powered purchase test cannot beat a simple measurement form plus existing visualization after return maturation.

ideas.title: Source a small assortment to satisfy unmet AI shopping constraints
ideas.buyer: Multi-brand retailers with flexible buying teams, small-lot suppliers and repeated unsatisfied shopping requests.
ideas.problem: Better metadata cannot create a product the merchant does not carry. Aggregate bestseller lists can miss a smaller but purchase-ready combination of requirements.
ideas.mechanism: Offer creation stage: group real unsatisfied requests by compatible constraints, estimate substitution and willingness to buy, and stock a limited set that covers those requests. Incremental purchases arise only if genuinely unmet demand materializes without merely displacing existing sales.
ideas.intervention: Build a demand-and-assortment optimizer that selects small pilot buys under inventory, working-capital and return constraints. Use observed merchant AI requests, explicit shopper feedback and historical substitution; separate absence of a suitable SKU from poor retrieval. Recommend concrete purchasable supplier SKUs with uncertain demand, not invented products or synthetic purchase intent.
ideas.competitorOverlap: Google Merchant Center already suggests popular products and brands to stock. Assortment and inventory optimization with substitution is established research. The proposed edge is exact unmet constraint combinations from AI-origin demand plus a controlled physical-stock pilot.
ideas.edgeHypothesis: A small inventory allocation chosen from repeated unsatisfied constraint sets creates more incremental retained purchasers per pound of inventory risk than the buyer's existing trend/popularity process.
dataNeeded: Real, deduplicated unsatisfied requests and their observed traffic source
Evidence that no existing SKU satisfies the request
Supplier catalogue, minimum order sizes, landed cost and replenishment lead time
Substitution/cannibalization history, retained orders and unsold inventory cost
ideas.experiment: Randomize matched, independently stocked region-category cells to an equal working-capital pilot selected by the optimizer or the existing buying process. Keep marketing support equal and predefine eligibility before inventory is added. Run at least one replenishment cycle, typically 12 weeks plus returns; require enough independent cells and account for stock spillovers. Primary endpoint is incremental retained purchasers among all eligible AI-origin category shoppers; guardrails are unsold stock, margin and fulfillment.
ideas.metric: ITT retained-purchaser probability across the whole category, with randomized cell inference. Report total contribution after carrying cost and cannibalization separately. Sales of the newly sourced SKU alone are not evidence of incremental demand.
ideas.impactEvidence: Hypothesized. google-assortment establishes the native alternative and assortment-paper a substitution-aware modelling precedent. Neither validates a market size or this tool's causal sales effect.

impactScenario.baseline: No assumed traffic or demand prevalence. Chosen sensitivity: GBP45 incremental contribution per retained shopper, GBP2,500 monthly software/operation cost and GBP1,000 monthly expected carrying/markdown cost.
impactScenario.calculation: (2,500 + 1,000)/45 = 77.78, so at least 78 incremental retained shoppers monthly before setup are needed. Absolute rate threshold is 77.78/N. A false demand signal can yield zero sales, negative incremental contribution and stranded inventory.

ideas.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated value-based pilot price: GBP2,000/month; inventory and buying labor are separate merchant costs. Seek a paid pilot only after proving sufficient unmet real demand.
ideas.costControl: Begin with small-lot suppliers and a few request clusters; stop buying when posterior demand cannot cover carrying cost. Reuse aggregate demand summaries rather than retaining unnecessary raw conversations.
dependencies: Real demand volume and supplier access
Independent inventory cells or another credible randomized stock design
Buyer authority and approved working-capital budget
ideas.failureMode: Requests express aspiration rather than willingness to pay, seasonality invalidates the estimate, or the new assortment cannibalizes better-margin products.
ideas.falsifier: Abandon if repeated small-stock pilots fail to outperform ordinary buying after category-wide cannibalization, return and carrying costs, even if the sourced SKUs sell.

ideas.title: Buy the missing product evidence with the highest decision value
ideas.buyer: Specialist merchants whose shoppers repeatedly hesitate over a fact absent from supplier data.
ideas.problem: A product assistant can retrieve every available document and still lack the decisive fact, such as sleeve opening width or the clearance needed to open a storage unit.
ideas.mechanism: Understanding and selection stages: identify factual uncertainty that blocks otherwise suitable candidates, obtain a real measurement or supplier confirmation, then make the result available during the decision. The enabling algorithm creates value only when acquired evidence changes actual retained purchases.
ideas.intervention: Build a value-of-information queue that ranks concrete evidence-acquisition tasks by affected real demand, probability the answer changes a shortlist, uncertainty and acquisition cost. Issue a precise measurement protocol to merchant staff or a supplier, validate units/provenance, and publish the factual result regardless of whether it is commercially favorable. Initial scope excludes safety-critical claims.
ideas.competitorOverlap: Constructor Product Insights already answers from product data, reviews and merchant content; Gorgias supports custom product facts; Lily Max scores and tests data gaps. The narrow difference is choosing and funding a new physical measurement or supplier investigation rather than extracting or rewriting existing information.
ideas.edgeHypothesis: A fixed evidence budget spent on facts that can change a real purchase decision produces more retained purchasers than a catalogue-completeness queue or existing gap scorer.
dataNeeded: Real unanswered shopper questions and feasible candidate sets
Existing supplier evidence and what remains genuinely unknown
Cost and reliability of each possible measurement
Auditable measurement results plus assigned-shopper orders and returns
ideas.experiment: Use two equally funded queues: decision-value selection versus the merchant's current missing-field priority. Assign product-family/store clusters before work and keep display treatment consistent. In a second randomized shopper test, compare newly measured factual answers with the current truthful information experience. Enroll for 8-12 weeks plus returns, with enough independent clusters for the queue comparison. Primary endpoint is category-wide retained purchasers, not resolved questions; check incorrect claims and cross-cluster spillover.
ideas.metric: ITT change in retained-purchaser probability for all eligible shoppers in assigned clusters; measure incremental contribution per pound of acquired evidence as a secondary efficiency result. Count unfavorable evidence that correctly disqualifies a product, and do not count successful measurements as sales.
ideas.impactEvidence: Hypothesized. constructor-pia, gorgias-data and lily-max show substantial overlap in answers and gap management. No source supports a conversion percentage or proves competitors lack this exact acquisition policy.

impactScenario.baseline: No observed traffic or blocked-demand proportion. Chosen sensitivity: GBP50 contribution per extra retained purchaser; GBP750 monthly fee and GBP500 monthly measurement labor.
impactScenario.calculation: (750 + 500)/50 = 25 additional retained purchasers monthly before setup. Required absolute purchase-rate gain is 25/N. A newly measured fact can reduce purchases, and evidence that resolves no material uncertainty has zero conversion value.

ideas.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated value-based test price: GBP750/month with an explicit separate evidence-work budget. A paid fixed-budget pilot is the demand test.
ideas.costControl: Acquire reusable family-level facts when valid, batch supplier questions, and stop acquiring evidence whose expected decision value is below its measured cost.
dependencies: Merchant or supplier access to measure the real product
A provenance workflow and category-specific measurement protocol
Enough repeated unanswered demand to justify acquisition
ideas.failureMode: The algorithm values frequently asked trivia, measurements vary between variants or production batches, or the merchant publishes only favorable results.
ideas.falsifier: Reject if targeted evidence does not beat a simple frequency-times-cost queue on retained purchases under equal spend, or if physical verification costs exceed the contribution recovered.

ideas.title: Allocate merchant changes by incremental purchase value under a fixed budget
ideas.buyer: Multi-store merchants and agencies with many credible improvements but limited engineering, experimentation and traffic budgets.
ideas.problem: A list of plausible changes can spend the full budget on interventions that improve simulated recommendation scores or clicks without creating additional purchasing shoppers.
ideas.mechanism: Experiment allocation stage: choose which deployable change to test next using expected incremental retained purchases, uncertainty, cost and reversibility. The resulting live changes must produce more purchases than an equally funded incumbent optimization workflow.
ideas.intervention: Build a budget-constrained policy over approved actions, such as compatibility answers, variant routing or checkout error repairs. Log action propensities and costs, use conservative offline estimates only where logged actions have support, retain a fixed randomized control, and promote actions only after mature order/refund outcomes. Treat simulation results as hypothesis features, never rewards.
ideas.competitorOverlap: Dynamic Yield already has bandit traffic allocation and purchase/revenue objectives. Shopify has SimGym and live Rollouts. Lily Max advertises an enrichment/test/deploy loop with holdouts. The proposed edge is resource allocation across distinct merchant actions with mature purchase outcomes and deployability constraints, not 'AI simulation plus A/B'.
ideas.edgeHypothesis: At equal total cost and experiment traffic, this policy finds and deploys more economically worthwhile improvements than a strong human/Lily-style prioritization process without materially worse shopper outcomes during learning.
dataNeeded: Approved action catalogue, eligibility, implementation cost and dependencies
Randomized action/exposure logs and exact policy probabilities
Per-store baseline purchase data and mature refunds
Audit of feed/page propagation where a change is externally consumed
ideas.experiment: Randomize matched merchant or independent store-category clusters to adaptive allocation versus a prespecified incumbent prioritization process, with equal cash/engineering budgets and a fixed shopper holdout inside each arm. Use at least a 12-week budget cycle plus order maturation; power by independent clusters, not simulation reruns. Primary endpoint is cumulative incremental retained purchasers versus each arm's holdout. Guardrails include returns, gross margin, latency and irreversible actions.
ideas.metric: Compare policy-level incremental retained purchasers per eligible shopper and total incremental purchasers within the same spend cap. Also report contribution net of implementation cost. A better off-policy value estimate or higher synthetic recommendation share is not a purchase result.
ideas.impactEvidence: Hypothesized. dr-policy supports an estimator family under assumptions; dy-allocation, dy-metric, lily-max, shopify-simgym and shopify-rollouts establish strong existing competition. No theoretical guarantee is transferred to sparse, delayed commerce outcomes.

impactScenario.baseline: No baseline traffic or uplift assumed. Chosen sensitivity: GBP50 contribution per additional retained purchaser and GBP2,500/month allocator plus extra operation cost over the comparator.
impactScenario.calculation: The allocator must cause at least 2,500/50 = 50 extra retained purchasers per month beyond the equally funded comparator, before setup. Absolute threshold is 50/N. If it merely picks the same actions later, value can be zero or negative.

ideas.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated value-based test price: GBP2,000/month for an agency or multi-store pilot; a small merchant is unlikely to provide enough experimental information.
ideas.costControl: Batch compatible actions, reject tests unable to reach a useful decision, and stop expensive replay once it no longer changes the live experiment choice.
dependencies: Enough independent merchants or clusters and mature outcomes
Logged propensities with support for candidate actions
Controlled deployment and rollback integrations
Agreement on fixed budgets and an always-held-out cohort
ideas.failureMode: Sparse delayed outcomes make the policy chase noise; poorly logged propensities invalidate offline estimates; interference between SKU changes makes apparent gains noncausal.
ideas.falsifier: Drop the policy if it cannot outperform prespecified expert prioritization under equal budgets across two powered budget cycles, or requires unsupported counterfactual extrapolation for most action choices.

ideas.title: Spend extra reasoning only when it can change a purchase decision
ideas.buyer: High-volume merchants operating a shopping assistant or approved agent tool with noticeable latency and inference cost.
ideas.problem: Uniformly expensive reasoning wastes time on easy requests, while a cheap model can fail on the small subset needing compatibility checks or fresh quotes.
ideas.mechanism: Decision and response stages: route easy, verified requests through a fast path and spend computation on ambiguous high-regret cases. Faster useful answers can prevent abandonment; retained savings can fund more valuable verification. Purchase preservation is a required constraint, not an assumed consequence of lower cost.
ideas.intervention: Build a calibrated decision-stability router using constraint coverage, evidence freshness, model disagreement and price/stock volatility. Actions are a deterministic lookup, a small model, an additional authoritative tool call or a stronger model. Assess whether the final product decision changes, and cap latency. Do not treat model self-confidence as calibrated truth.
ideas.competitorOverlap: FrugalGPT and RouteLLM already study cost-aware cascades and routing. Merchant assistants already choose content sources. The edge hypothesis is a commerce-specific objective and guardrails based on real retained purchases and exact decision errors.
ideas.edgeHypothesis: Against both always-expensive reasoning and a simple rule-based router, decision-stability routing maintains or improves retained-purchaser rate while reducing cost and response delay. Savings alone are insufficient if purchases fall.
dataNeeded: Request class and exact evidence/tool state
Outputs, latency and cost from candidate execution paths
Human-verified decision errors on a held-out category set
Assigned-shopper purchases, cancellations and returns
ideas.experiment: Persistently randomize eligible assistant shoppers to router, always-strong execution or a simple deterministic router. Start after blinded offline decision-error checks. Run 6-8 weeks plus returns, powered for a prespecified purchase noninferiority margin and superiority if faster responses are claimed to increase purchases. Guardrails include factual/compatibility errors, timeout rate and contribution per shopper.
ideas.metric: Primary is retained purchasers divided by every assigned eligible shopper. Cost per retained purchaser and p95 answer latency are secondary. Claim incremental purchases only if the randomized purchase contrast is positive with appropriate uncertainty; otherwise report a bounded cost tradeoff.
ideas.impactEvidence: Hypothesized commerce effect. routellm and frugalgpt establish adjacent routing methods, not current-model savings or shopping conversion lift.

impactScenario.baseline: No observed traffic, latency or conversion assumed. Sensitivity uses S for measured monthly inference savings, GBP600/month fee/operations and GBP40 contribution per changed retained purchaser.
impactScenario.calculation: Net contribution = S + 40*delta_retained_purchasers - 600 - amortized_setup. For illustration only, if S=GBP1,000, cost breaks even at delta=-10 before setup; the purchase-preservation guardrail can still reject that loss. With S=0, 15 extra retained purchasers are needed. Zero or negative purchase effects must be reported.

ideas.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated value-based test price: GBP400/month plus usage, or a capped share of audited savings only after purchase noninferiority is established.
ideas.costControl: This is the cost lever: cached verified lookups, bounded tool calls and selective larger-model use. Reinvest only demonstrable savings into experiments that can generate more purchases.
dependencies: Merchant controls execution and can observe model/tool costs
Enough traffic to detect a meaningful conversion loss
Category-specific independent decision-error labels
ideas.failureMode: The router is confident on difficult cases, cached facts become stale, or extra routing overhead erases latency savings.
ideas.falsifier: Reject if the router breaches the purchase/error noninferiority limits, or a static two-rule cascade matches its cost and conversion with less complexity.

ideas.title: Explore new products only among verified suitable choices
ideas.buyer: Retailers with frequent new launches or a long tail of genuinely suitable SKUs underexposed in AI-assisted shopping.
ideas.problem: Purchase-trained rankings can keep showing familiar items because new products lack observations. Blind promotion of new items can displace better choices without increasing the number of buyers.
ideas.mechanism: Discovery within the merchant-controlled choice set: cautiously expose a suitable cold-start item when evidence suggests it may satisfy an unmet preference, learn from actual orders and returns, and reduce exposure if the portfolio outcome worsens.
ideas.intervention: Build a constrained contextual exploration policy over one optional shortlist slot. Every candidate must first meet the shopper's hard requirements and live availability. Use logged randomization, a fixed incumbent holdout and a bounded risk budget; optimize all-category retained purchasers rather than new-SKU sales, clicks or supplier payments.
ideas.competitorOverlap: Algolia already has hybrid cold-start recommendations and rules that pin new items. Conservative contextual bandits are established research. The edge is verified eligibility plus purchase-level incremental exploration with delayed returns, not 'discover new products with AI'.
ideas.edgeHypothesis: A bounded exploration slot finds underexposed suitable products that increase retained purchasing shoppers relative to a tuned hybrid recommender and manual launch pinning, with acceptable short-term downside.
dataNeeded: New/underexposed SKU attributes and evidence-backed eligibility
Explicit shopper task/context without sensitive inference
Exposure probabilities, position and accepted/rejected choices
All-category orders, returns and contribution over the full assignment window
ideas.experiment: Randomize shoppers before shortlist construction to exploration, the tuned incumbent hybrid policy or manual launch pinning. Keep list length and incentives equal, persist assignments and retain a fixed holdout while the policy learns. Run 8-12 weeks plus returns; delayed rewards and small launch cohorts may require several launch cycles. Primary endpoint is all-category retained-purchaser probability; stop on prespecified downside limits.
ideas.metric: Unique retained purchasers divided by all unique assigned eligible shoppers, with persistent shopper assignment and the shopper as analysis unit. New-SKU exposure and sales are diagnostics. Incrementality excludes purchases merely transferred from existing SKUs.
ideas.impactEvidence: Hypothesized. algolia-coldstart and algolia-rules establish direct competition; conservative-bandit offers a formal precursor under assumptions that do not guarantee live commerce safety.

impactScenario.baseline: No measured launch traffic or conversion baseline. Chosen sensitivity: GBP40 contribution per added retained purchaser and GBP900/month total recurring cost.
impactScenario.calculation: 900/40 = 22.5, so at least 23 extra retained purchasers monthly before setup. Absolute break-even gain is 22.5/N. New-SKU sales can rise with zero incremental buyers; displacement or wrong choices can make the effect negative.

ideas.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated value-based test price: GBP750/month for a high-launch-volume merchant, after a comparison against their already-licensed recommender.
ideas.costControl: Explore only a bounded verified candidate set, pool evidence across genuine shared attributes, and retire candidates when expected learning value no longer justifies shopper exposure.
dependencies: Control over merchant assistant/landing recommendation slots
Strong incumbent benchmark and hard-constraint validation
Propensity logging and mature delayed reward handling
ideas.failureMode: The policy mistakes novelty clicks for new demand, weakens choice quality during learning or merely reallocates purchases among SKUs.
ideas.falsifier: Reject if multiple launch cycles show increased new-SKU sales without a worthwhile all-category retained-purchaser increase, or if the incumbent hybrid recommender performs as well with less risk.

sources.title: Shopping with ChatGPT Search
sources.claim: Explains product and merchant selection factors and Shopify Catalog integration. A merchant-controlled retrieval policy does not establish control over ChatGPT ranking.

sources.title: Get Started
sources.claim: Documents approved-partner feed onboarding and full snapshots plus API updates. Feed acceptance is not consumer-surface exposure or purchase evidence.

sources.title: Learn about AI Shopping Agent
sources.claim: Documents goal-based conversations, refinement, multi-item recommendations and clickstream feedback. Establishes direct competitive overlap, not an audited purchase effect.

sources.title: AI Ecommerce Search and Product Discovery | Constructor
sources.claim: Lists Answer Engine Assistants beta for real-time discovery and purchase data. Availability and exact guarantees need commercial verification.

sources.title: A Constraint-based Recommender System via RDF Knowledge Graphs
sources.claim: Demonstrates knowledge-graph constraint recommendation in vehicle selection. Research feasibility does not establish incremental ecommerce purchases.

sources.title: EComAgentBench: Benchmarking Shopping Agents on Long-Horizon Tasks with Distributed Hidden Intent
sources.claim: Uses 662 product-grounded tasks with visible queries, tool-gated profiles and scripted clarification. Its benchmark accuracy is not human purchase conversion.

sources.title: Learning to Ask Appropriate Questions in Conversational Recommendation
sources.claim: Studies question selection in conversational recommendation. Supports a technical precursor, without evidence for this proposed live purchase policy.

sources.title: ComboShoppingBench: Evaluating LLM Agents for Budget-Constrained Basket Shopping with Coupons
sources.claim: Simulated basket tasks jointly test compatibility, availability, coupons and budgets with deterministic checks. Establishes an offline evaluation pattern only.

sources.title: Frequently Bought Together Recommendations - “Strict” Mode
sources.claim: Algolia already offers co-purchase recommendation restricted to items actually bought together. Co-purchase is not proof of whole-basket technical compatibility.

sources.title: Merchandise Recommendations
sources.claim: Documents filtering out-of-stock recommendations and pinning newly launched products. These basic interventions are established capabilities.

sources.title: Co-op: Scaling Grocery Search and Improving Basket Sizes With Algolia
sources.claim: Documents an implemented out-of-stock recommendation experience and vendor-reported results. It does not establish a randomized AI-origin purchase effect for the proposed policy.

sources.title: RoomPlan Overview - Augmented Reality - Apple Developer
sources.claim: RoomPlan uses camera and LiDAR to output parametric room and furniture dimensions. It supplies geometry, not a guarantee that a purchased item will fit.

sources.title: Can I resize an item or adjust the dimensions of the room in IKEA Kreativ?
sources.claim: IKEA already provides scaled furniture placement with scans, photos and manually defined rooms. Its vendor accuracy description is not independent fit or conversion validation.

sources.title: About popular products in Merchant Center Analytics
sources.claim: Google provides popular-product and brand suggestions to guide assortment and stock decisions. Aggregate popularity differs from an observed unsatisfied constraint set.

sources.title: Joint assortment and inventory planning for heavy tailed demand
sources.claim: Studies joint assortment and inventory with substitution, including computational experiments. It does not prove purchase uplift for a new merchant tool.

sources.title: Learn about Product Insights Agent
sources.claim: Documents product answers grounded in catalogue data, reviews and merchant content. A basic product-question assistant is direct existing competition.

sources.title: Manage your product information for AI Agent
sources.claim: Documents Shopify, storefront and custom product information for AI answers. A missing-field editor is already available.

sources.title: Dynamic Allocation
sources.claim: Documents adaptive multi-armed-bandit allocation. Generic traffic allocation is established competition.

sources.title: Choosing a Primary Metric
sources.claim: Dynamic Yield supports purchase and revenue metrics for experiments and allocation. A purchase objective alone is not a novel distinction.

sources.title: How Lily Max Works | Agentic Product Intelligence
sources.claim: Advertises gap detection, enrichment, controlled testing, holdouts, difference-in-differences and approved deployment. Public marketing does not establish randomized causal validity for every implementation.

sources.title: Shopify Help Center | SimGym
sources.claim: Native synthetic shoppers compare themes with add-to-cart and qualitative feedback. Shopify explicitly notes differences from actual buyer behavior.

sources.title: Shopify Help Center | Types of rollouts and changes
sources.claim: Documents native treatment/control experiments on eligible plans and resources. Basic live A/B testing is not a gap.

sources.title: Doubly Robust Policy Evaluation and Learning
sources.claim: Combines reward and action-policy models for offline evaluation. Logged action support, valid propensities and assumptions still matter.

sources.title: RouteLLM: Learning to Route LLMs with Preference Data
sources.claim: Studies learned model routing with preference data. General task results cannot quantify shopping conversion or current-model savings.

sources.title: FrugalGPT: How to Use Large Language Models While Reducing Cost and Improving Performance
sources.claim: Studies cost-sensitive model cascades on language tasks. It does not prove a safe commerce latency or purchase tradeoff.

sources.title: Algolia Launches Additional AI Models in its Recommend Spring Release 2022 to Supercharge Businesses Ability to Engage with Users
sources.claim: Documents hybrid content and behavioral recommendations for cold-start items. Cold-start retrieval alone is an existing feature.

sources.title: Conservative Contextual Linear Bandits
sources.claim: Provides conservative exploration under a contextual linear model and baseline-performance assumptions. Its theoretical guarantees do not automatically cover nonstationary delayed-return commerce.
